# Our two-year bond is enough to begin

Lend 100 today, receive coupon 5 at year one and coupon 5 plus principal 100 at year two. If the appropriate yield is 5% and compounded yearly, its price is 100. That one object lets us study almost every major concept in fixed income.

## The learning path

### First: understand prices and market quotes

1. [Interactive Bond Pricing](bond-pricing.qmd) — move the yield and watch the bond price respond.
2. [Coupon, Current Yield and YTM](02-yield-and-total-return.qmd) — three percentages that mean different things.
3. [Clean/Dirty Price and Accrued Interest](03-clean-dirty-and-accrued.qmd) — quoted price versus actual settlement cash.

### Next: each future date has its own rate

4. [Spot Rates and Discount Factors](04-spot-rates-and-discount-factors.qmd) — price cash one date at a time.
5. [Curve Bootstrapping](05-curve-bootstrapping.qmd) — recover an unknown curve point from bond prices.
6. [Forward Rates](06-forward-rates.qmd) — a second-year rate implied by today's term structure.

### Then: how much can the price move?

7. [Duration](duration.qmd) — first-order sensitivity to yield.
8. [Convexity](07-convexity.qmd) — why the price/yield curve bends.
9. [DV01 and Key-Rate Risk](08-dv01-and-key-rate-risk.qmd) — risk in money and by maturity bucket.
10. [Immunisation and Liability Matching](09-immunization-and-liability-matching.qmd) — protect a future payment obligation.

### Finally: the contractual cash flow might change

11. [Credit Spread, Default and Recovery](10-credit-spreads-default-recovery.qmd) — promises are not always paid.
12. [Callable Bonds, MBS and OAS](11-callable-mbs-and-oas.qmd) — changing rates can change the cash flows themselves.
13. [Carry and Roll-Down](12-carry-and-roll-down.qmd) — returns from coupons and the passage of time.
14. [Floating-Rate Notes](13-floating-rate-notes.qmd) — coupons that reset as reference rates change.

## Read this before more complicated risk equations

For the fixed two-year bond, a higher discount rate reduces the present value of BOTH future receipts. That gives the fundamental inverse price–yield relationship. Duration describes its local slope. Convexity describes how that slope changes. Key-rate duration generalises the risk to a curve with many independently moving points.

**But:** if interest rate changes cause prepayments, calls or defaults, treating all future payments as fixed is no longer correct. That is why effective duration and model-dependent OAS exist.

**Textbook route:** Fabozzi, *Handbook*, 8th ed., Chapters 1–2, 6–8, 12, 17 and 40–41; Luenberger, *Investment Science*, 2nd ed., Chapters 2–4, 16–17.
